A:bd-william-lavina-clark:f.note: Headstone, Clark-Whobrey Cemetery, Roundhill, Edmonson Co., Ky.: 'born Oct. the 13 1785 ... departed this life Jan. 6 1856 on sunday morning'.

A:gaunt-peter:father.note: Husband of Lydia Gaunt and probable father of Hananiah. Their family is described by Sandwich Friends historical research and the published Barnstable probate abstract of Lydia's will. Exact birth/death dates and Lincoln ancestry remain unresolved; do not substitute the speculative Hampton maiden surname for Lydia.

A:gaunt-lydia:mother.note: Her will dated 28 Dec 1691 and proved 21 Apr 1692 explicitly names sons Israel, Zachariah and Hannaniah, plus daughter Lydia and grandchildren. Source: Barnstable probate records 1:66–67, abstracted by Gustavus Adolphus Hinckley, as transcribed on WeRelate. Published abstract accessed live; original probate image not accessed. Maiden surname unknown.21 Apr 1692 is the probate date, not an established death date.

A:benjamin-hulsey:father.note: The original 1880 census records B. F. Hulsey, a thirty-two-year-old miner born in Georgia, with wife Sarah G., 30, born Arkansas, and son George W., 4, in Center Township, Montgomery County, Arkansas. George’s December 1875 birth in the 1900 Sulphur Springs census and 24 December 1875 birth on his 1918 draft card are consistent with the child’s age. An unsourced 1977 family query links a Benjamin F. to George Washington, but contains conflicting names and dates and does not prove the connection. The connection remains probable: no record yet explicitly connects the adult George, husband of Sarah Rebecca Graves, to the named 1880 parents. This household has not been securely identified with the separate Benjamin Franklin Hulsey biography or with Sylvania Partain.

A:balas-newton:father.note: The original 1889 Etowah County marriage papers identify Balas Newton as Lizzie Newton’s father. The 1880 Etowah census lists Balus Newton and daughter Elizabeth, aged seven; its rare name, place and age make this a probable match, although the census and marriage papers do not contain a second unique identifier. The census lists his wife Mary; her identification as Lizzie’s mother is probable.

A:sarah-g-hulsey:mother.note: The original 1880 census lists Sarah G., 30, born Arkansas, as the wife of B. F. Hulsey, in the household containing his son George W., 4. She is a probable mother or stepmother of that child; the census names her as wife, not explicitly as his biological mother. The identification of this child with the later George Washington Hulsey remains probable. Hulsey is her married surname; her maiden name and full given names are unknown. She is not Sarah Rebecca Graves, George’s later wife, and has not been identified with Sylvania Susane Partain.

A:bridget-croasdale:mother.note: Potts (1895), p. 29, lists Bridget among Thomas and Agnes Croasdale’s children, using birth dates supplied from Settle Monthly Meeting; the book notes that Middletown dates vary. The Middletown register transcription names John and Bridget as Elizabeth Cowgill’s parents. The original meeting-register image has not yet been independently reread. The connection is marked probable.

A:thomas-croasdale:father.note: Potts (1895), pp. 25–29, reproduces the Settle certificate, estate inventory and children’s list. The inventory supports a 1684 death; the 1682 date in some later accounts conflicts with it. His own birth date and parentage have not been established from an independently examined original register.

A:agnes-hawthornthwaite:mother.note: Potts (1895) gives Agnes’s marriage to Thomas, names her in the Settle certificate and reproduces her estate inventory. Her surname appears in variant forms, including Hathernthwaite. The printed inventory date conflicts with the reported death and administration chronology; that inconsistency remains unresolved. Her parents are not attached.

A:thomas-mercer:father.note: The original Ringwood Quaker birth entry, TNA RG6/1027 image 18/206, handwritten p. 6, has been visually reviewed and names Thomas and Ann Mercer of Ringwood as parents of Ann, born on the 24th day of the 12th month 1666 (24 Feb 1666/7). Identifying this child with the later Pennsylvania wife of William Brown, and this father with Thomas of Andover/Aston, remains probable. His own parents are unknown. The 1709 Yearly Meeting catalogue, independently read in its 1979 printed transcription (PGM31:120), directly names the immigrant Anne Browne as Thomas Mercer’s daughter and says she came with him. It remembers her among deceased Public Friends; the original manuscript has not been examined. The Ringwood-to-immigrant identification remains probable.

A:ann-mercer:mother.note: The original Ringwood birth register names Ann and Thomas Mercer of Ringwood as the parents of the child Ann, born on the 24th day of the 12th month 1666 (24 Feb 1666/7). No maiden surname is given. Identification with the mother of William Brown’s later Pennsylvania wife remains probable. Her maiden surname and life dates remain unknown; Mercer is not asserted as her maiden surname.

A:richard-browne:father.note: The original Wellingborough birth register, TNA RG6/1380 image 20/150, names Richard Browne as Willyam’s father, with birth on the 29th day of the first month 1658. It names no mother. This register entry has been visually reviewed; the Northamptonshire Quarterly Meeting entry and the varying maternal names in later accounts remain to be checked. Identifying the English child with the Pennsylvania emigrant remains probable. No earlier parents or exact life dates are assigned to Richard.

A:margaret-m-hulsey:1880.note: Recorded as a child of B. F. Hulsey in the 1880 Center Township household, Montgomery County, Arkansas. Margaret was six and Charles five months old. They are probable siblings of the later George Washington Hulsey because identification of the four-year-old George in this household with the adult George remains probable. Sarah G. is recorded as the wife of the household head, not explicitly as the children’s biological mother; no mother is attached here. This child has not been merged with a similarly named person in the 1900 census.

A:charles-f-hulsey:1880.note: Recorded as a child of B. F. Hulsey in the 1880 Center Township household, Montgomery County, Arkansas. Margaret was six and Charles five months old. They are probable siblings of the later George Washington Hulsey because identification of the four-year-old George in this household with the adult George remains probable. Sarah G. is recorded as the wife of the household head, not explicitly as the children’s biological mother; no mother is attached here. This child has not been merged with a similarly named person in the 1900 census.

A:joel-john-thompson:brother.note: Dawes Card 1283 records this child in Joseph P. and Betsy Thompson’s household and refers the parents to the first two entries. Joel’s 1937 Indian-Pioneer interview names those parents and supplies his birth date. His death date appears on the shared Joel John and Ira Mae Thompson headstone. The young studio portrait is attributed by an Ancestry tree tag, not an inscription on this crop.

A:peter-pitchlynn-thompson:brother.note: Dawes Card 1283 records this child in Joseph P. and Betsy Thompson’s household and refers the parents to the first two entries. Joel’s 1937 interview names his brother Peter Pitchlyn. The approximate birth and 1979 death year come from the High Hill cemetery transcription; that stone remains to be checked independently.

A:ella-n-thompson:sister.note: Dawes Card 1283 records this child in Joseph P. and Betsy Thompson’s household and refers the parents to the first two entries. Joseph’s 13 April 1901 sworn affidavit identifies Ella as his daughter and gives her death as 22 May 1899. Her birth is estimated from the age on the card.

A:edith-irene-thompson:sister.note: Her family memorial in the May 2012 Biskinik, p. 16, names her parents as Simon and Francis Thompson and her deceased brother Junior. Francis is the spelling printed in the memorial; the mother is recorded elsewhere as Frances Pisachubbe.

A:james-calvin-stevenson.note: Elam Stevenson’s will and the Goodspeed family sketch name both James C. and Abner A. as sons of Elam. The 1912 Andrews autobiography names James C. and Margaret C. as Eliza Catherine Stevenson’s parents.

A:margaret-caroline-brown.note: The 1912 autobiography by her son-in-law W. T. Andrews names Margaret C. Stevenson as Eliza Catherine’s mother. Her maiden name and dates are from published family histories; her parents are not attached.

A:eliza-catherine-stevenson.note: Her husband W. T. Andrews named her parents and their son James David in his 1912 autobiography. James David’s 1937 obituary independently names William Thomas and Eliza Stevenson Andrews as his parents.

A:william-thomas-andrews.note: In his 1912 autobiography he identifies his wife Eliza Catherine Stevenson, her parents James C. and Margaret C., and their son James David.

A:james-david-andrews.note: His father’s 1912 autobiography names him, and his 1937 Pulaski Citizen obituary names his parents and son Major General Frank M. Andrews. Nashville Public Library’s family papers identify Frank Maxwell Andrews as a son of James David and Lula Maxwell.

A:lula-adaline-maxwell.note: Nashville Public Library’s finding aid identifies Lula Adaline Maxwell Andrews and James D. Andrews as Frank Maxwell Andrews’s parents.

A:frank-maxwell-andrews.note: James David’s obituary names his son Major General Frank M. Andrews; Nashville Public Library’s family papers identify him as Frank Maxwell Andrews. W. T. Andrews’s own 1912 memoir names James David’s mother and grandparents, connecting this branch to Elam and Lydia Stevenson.

A:mary-dockery:newton.note: Mary Ann Dockery married Bailus Newton in 1867. The 1880 census records Balus Newton, wife Mary and a daughter Elizabeth, seven. Their identification with Lizzie Newton and her father Balas, named in the 1889 marriage papers, is probable; the census does not explicitly say Mary was Elizabeth’s mother. An Alabama death index names Mary Marzee Dockery as the mother of Oda Verbena Newton, a possible match for the youngest child in the household.

A:john-satterfield-1766.note: His will (Warren Co., Ky., Will Book D, p. 262, proved 10 Nov 1847) names Ephraim among thirteen children; Ephraim's son Henry's 1861 death register names Ephraim and Rutha as parents, which ties the line (probable). The will names a wife Mary but does not say she was Ephraim's mother, so no mother link is added. John's own father is disputed and not entered.

A:ruth-knowles-satterfield.note: Married Ephraim Satterfield 12 Nov 1809, Warren Co., Ky. Henry Satterfield's Kentucky death register entry (24 Dec 1861) names his parents as Ephraim and 'Rutha' Satterfield. Her father Joshua Knowles's 1824 will names 'Ruth Saterfield' among his daughters. Both seen through WikiTree transcriptions (probable).

A:joshua-knowles.note: Will dated 11 Nov 1824, proved Oct 1832, names wife Jemima and daughter 'Ruth Saterfield'. Whether Jemima was Ruth's mother is not stated, so no mother is entered.

A:william-croasdale-newhey.dp: Newhey, Forest of Bowland, Yorkshire, England
A:william-croasdale-newhey.note: Buried at the Friends' burial ground of Settle Meeting. The Welcome Society reference work, Patterson's list of Quaker emigrants and the family genealogist Cleaver ('highly probable') make him father of the 1682 emigrant Thomas Croasdale; secondary sources only (probable). His father, possibly Henry Croasdale of Newhey, is a lead and is not linked.

A:elizabeth-croasdale-newhey.note: Wife of William Croasdale, buried beside him at Settle Meeting. Her maiden surname is often given as Hayhurst, but no original record names it, so it is left off her name here.

A:ellen-cowgill.note: Settle Monthly Meeting certificate of 7 June 1682 lists 'Ellen Cowgill widow & her children'; John Cowgill, who married Bridget Croasdale in 1693, is identified as her son by the Cowgill family studies (probable). Her husband's name and her maiden name are not documented.

xf1-001.note: Private in the North Carolina militia, discharged near Stono 2 Jul 1779 and at Frederick County, Maryland, 14 Jan 1782 (pension file S 31049, as summarized in Stuart's 1979 Garrison compilation). Married Esther Alexander 14 Mar 1786, Mecklenburg Co. His father is unresolved: two different John Garrisons are proposed and neither is proved.

xf1-002.note: Named as 'Esther Garrison' in her father Hezekiah Alexander's will of 8 Aug 1796, with a daughter Caroline Garrison (American Monthly Magazine, Apr 1913, p. 188). Her husband's name, Samuel Garrison, comes from the Garrison family record. Birth is 23 or 28 September 1762 and death 1827 or 1829 in Stuart's text; WikiTree places her death in Coles County, Illinois, which the family record does not support.

xf1-003.note: Mecklenburg magistrate, patriot and elder of Sugar Creek church; will dated 8 Aug 1796. Birth 13 Jan 1722 per Stuart, 1728 per the Dictionary of North Carolina Biography; death 10 Jan 1801 per Stuart, 16 Jul 1801 per the dictionary. The link from his daughter Esther to John Milton Garrison is probable.

xf1-004.note: Married Hezekiah Alexander 12 Jun 1752 (Dictionary of North Carolina Biography). Named as his wife and executor in his 1796 will. Stuart gives her death as 17 May 1806 at 71; an earlier note on this site has 1805.

xf1-005.note: Eldest child in the Garrison family record; married William Ray in 1814. Named as 'dau. Caroline Garrison' in her grandfather Hezekiah Alexander's will of 8 Aug 1796.

xf1-006.bp: Cowan Ford, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina
xf1-006.note: Married Rebecca Lyle 10 Jun 1813, Warren Co., Ky.; moved to Morgan County, Alabama. Birth day is 8 or 18 February in Stuart's text.

xf1-007.note: Born at her grandfather Hezekiah Alexander's home, per the family record. Nothing further found.

xf1-008.bp: Mallard Creek, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina
xf1-008.note: Married Eliza Pogue 23 Jun 1829 and Chalia S. (Mitchell) Jones 10 Dec 1840. Birth day is 21 or 25 September in Stuart's text.

xf1-009.bp: Bays Fork Creek, Warren County, Kentucky
xf1-009.note: Married Mariah Neal and later Nancy Margaret Hawkins, per the family record.

xf1-010.bp: Bays Fork Creek, Warren County, Kentucky
xf1-010.note: Married Samuel Alfred Stubbins 4 Aug 1825; three daughters and an infant son (born 13 Nov, died 3 Dec 1831).

xf1-011.bp: Bays Fork Creek, Warren County, Kentucky
xf1-011.note: Married John C. McPheeters 22 Jun 1825. Middle name is spelled Wilson or Willison in Stuart's text.

xf1-013.bp: Pennsylvania-Maryland line (his pension statement); Cecil County, Maryland
xf1-013.note: Physician and Revolutionary War sergeant and surgeon; son of Hezekiah Alexander named in his 1796 will. Married Dorcas Garrison 26 Nov 1789 (York District, S.C.). Birth is from his own 1833 pension statement as summarized by Holliman; the 1836 death date is from a search snippet of a 1989 Simpson County history and is unconfirmed, and Holliman has only 'after 1832.'

xf1-012.note: Son of Nathan Moffitt and Rebecca Williams by the household at Strawberry Township, Lawrence Co., Ark. (see the story on this site). A research guide names a Calvin V. Moffitt of Lawrence County who served in two Arkansas Confederate units and then sought a Union pension; the identification is probable.

xf2-001.note: The birth affidavit of 29 April 1905 and Newborn Card 1410, as told in the linked story, name Joseph P. and Betsy Thompson as his parents. The Dawes final roll index lists Joseph W. Thompson on Newborn Card 1410 (index only).

xf2-002.note: The 1891 sketch of Joseph P. Thompson (O'Beirne, p. 162) names Alexander, born in March 1890, as his one child by Betsey Ann Tims. The Dawes final roll index lists Alexander B. Thompson on Card 1283 with Joseph P. and Betsy Thompson (index only), and Joel Thompson's 1937 interview names Alex B. first among his brothers and sisters. No later record has been found.

xf2-003.note: Listed with Emiline Tims on Dawes Card 778 (final roll index, index only). This site's story on Betsy Thompson names John and Calvin among her brothers. The index prints ages 29 (Johnny) and 17 (Calvin); on the other Tims cards checked, the index age runs three years above the 1899 card age, so these birth years are estimates. No record of his later life has been found.

xf2-004.note: Listed with Emiline Tims on Dawes Card 778 (final roll index, index only), with the same limits as his brother Johnny. This site's story on Betsy Thompson names Calvin among her brothers. No record of his later life has been found.

xf2-005.note: The 1941 Methodist Indian Mission memoir gives his birth at Doaksville on 25 June 1864 and his age as 77 at death; Dawes Card 510 names his parents as Vinson W. and Emeline Tims. The year of death is inferred from the memoir, as the linked story explains.

xf2-006.note: Dawes Card 850 names his parents as 'Benson Tims,' dead, and Emiline Tims, the same couple that other cards spell Vinson and Vincent. The 1950 death year and the High Hill burial are given in the linked stories.

xf2-007.note: Dawes Card 1268 names his parents as Vincent Tims, dead, and Emiline Tims. Birth year estimated from the card age of 23 in 1899.

xf2-008.note: Enrolled first on her mother's Card 778 and moved to her husband James Wilson's Card 1281 in October 1900; a notary's letter of 19 October 1900 identifies her as the daughter of Emiline Tims. Birth year estimated from the card age of 18 in 1899.

xf2-009.note: His 1944 memoir in the Methodist Indian Mission minutes names his parents as Vincent and Emiline Tims and gives his death on 12 September 1944; Dawes Card 816 gives his age as 25 in 1899.

xf2-010.note: Dawes Card 1437 names his parents as Vincent B. Tims and Betsy Tims, both dead. Birth year and death date follow the linked story; he is buried at Springs Chapel Cemetery near Hugo.

xf2-011.note: Second wife of Edward Ward Tims; they married on 29 April 1888 (certificate in the Dawes jacket). Her dates come from a grave memorial cited in the Edward Ward Tims story and fit her December 1902 testimony giving her age as 32. Her parents are not named; her father Maxwell is marked a non-citizen on Card 1437.

xf2-012.note: Son of Edward W. Tims and Willie Jane on Dawes Card 1437 (listed as Edmund, 3, on the 1896 census). The 36th Division honor roll gives his death as 8 October 1918 and the regiment's report as the morning of the 9th; the date here follows the report.

xf2-013.note: Dawes Card 1580 names Joseph Pisachubbe, dead, as his father and Eunice as his mother, and the 1927 estate petition calls him and Robert her lawful issue. Birth year from the card age of 16 in 1899; death in May 1937 from the Hugo Daily News obituary cited in the linked story.

xf2-014.note: Dawes Card 1363 (Roll 3740) and the affidavit her mother Molsey swore on 19 April 1901 name Legion Austin as her father. She later married William Harrison Pisachubbe, brother of her sister Lizzie's husband Robert, as the linked story tells.

xf2-015.note: His father's affidavit on Dawes Card 1363 gives his birth on 15 November 1898; the card notes that he died in April 1899, before enrollment.

xf2-016.note: Child of George Washington Hulsey and Sarah Rebecca Graves in the family listing of their ten children, as told in the linked story. Eldest of the ten; listed in the 1910 census household in Mountain Township, Garland County, Arkansas. Later life not traced.

xf2-017.note: Child of George Washington Hulsey and Sarah Rebecca Graves in the family listing of their ten children, as told in the linked story. Listed as John W. in the 1910 census household. Later life not traced.
